mainTopic: מוקצה of wood on יום טוב (props, sticks, skewers, pokers) and the משנה forbidding a new fire
overview: This amud begins by finishing a list of things that may be set up on יום טוב only if the top is held first and the supports are added after. It then turns to the משנה's rule that one may not prop a pot, or a door, with a log. A ברייתא explains that wood is set aside only for burning, so any other use is מוקצה, while רבי שמעון permits. Leading an animal with a stick is forbidden even by רבי שמעון, because it looks like a weekday trip to market. רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about using a bamboo branch as a roasting skewer, and after two versions of their dispute the הלכה is that a dry branch is permitted and a wet one is forbidden. רבא then teaches two rules about a fire-poker. The גמרא shows these fit with his feeding goose innards to the cat, since innards spoil and were intended for the animals from before יום טוב. A new משנה follows. It records רבי אליעזר and חכמים arguing over gathering kindling from the courtyard, then forbids making a brand-new fire or heating tiles white-hot for roasting. The גמרא's discussion of that משנה, opened by רב יהודה, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The same building order applies to eggs, a pot, a bed, and barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא extends the rule it just gave about the right order for setting things up on יום טוב to four more items.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true of eggs, and of a pot, and of a bed, and of barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the end of the previous section. The same 'hold the top first, then put the supports underneath' method applies to eggs, a pot, a folding bed, and stacked barrels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא taught that a temporary structure may be set up on יום טוב only if the top piece is held in place first and the supports are added afterward. Done that way, it does not look like building. This line adds four everyday cases where the same method works.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly / and the same applies
A bed (here, a folding bed made of separate pieces)

steps.confusionAlert: This line has no new rule of its own. It only makes sense as the end of the previous discussion about the order of setting up things on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And similarly eggs, and similarly a pot,
phrases.notes: Eggs are placed on the vessel first, then the vessel is set on the coals. The pot is held up before the barrels are placed under it.

phrases.english: and similarly a bed, and similarly barrels.
phrases.notes: The top of the bed is held out first and the legs are added after. The upper barrel is held first and the lower ones are put beneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues earlier's rule about building order on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs, a pot, a folding bed, and stacked barrels must all be set up with the top held first and the supports added afterward.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: no propping a pot with a log
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a pot may not be propped up with a piece of firewood, 'and similarly with a door.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] One may not prop up a pot with a log, and similarly with a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next move, because the words 'with a door' sound odd.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that firewood may not be used as a prop for a pot on יום טוב. The extra phrase 'and similarly with a door' is what the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.english: And one may not prop up the pot with a log,
and similarly with a door.
phrases.notes: This wording is what the גמרא challenges next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Firewood may not be used to prop up a pot on יום טוב.

steps.title: Who would prop a pot with a door?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's wording cannot mean propping a pot with a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With a door'? Could that even enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. Nobody holds up a pot by leaning a door against it, so the phrase cannot mean what it seems to say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'and similarly with a door' means using a door to prop the pot. That is not a realistic case, so the wording needs to be read differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a sign the reading seems impossible)

phrases.english: With a door, could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last phrase of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וכן בדלת' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the phrase describes using a door to prop a pot, which no one actually does.

steps.title: Correct the wording: the door is what gets propped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the phrase as 'and similarly a door,' meaning a door may not be propped open with a log.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'and similarly a door' [may not be propped with a log].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by fixing the wording. The door is not the prop. It is the thing being propped, and a log may not be used to hold it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change moves the door from being the tool to being the object. Now the rule matches the first case: firewood may not serve as a support, whether for a pot or for a door.

phrases.english: Rather, say: and similarly the door.
phrases.notes: The door is also not to be propped with a log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The door is the tool used to prop the pot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The door is the thing being propped, and a log may not be used to prop it.

steps.title: The ברייתא's reason: wood is only for burning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the rule and explains it: wood is set aside only for burning, so using it as a prop is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: One may not prop up a pot with a log, and similarly a door, because wood was given only for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the reason behind the משנה's rule. Firewood counts as 'for burning only,' so any other use is off-limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Firewood is ready to use on יום טוב only for fuel. For anything else, like propping a pot or a door, it is מוקצה. The ברייתא also supports the corrected reading 'וכן הדלת.'

keyTerms.meaning: Wood was given (designated) only for burning
Set aside, so it may not be handled or used

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that 'wood is only for burning' is the key principle for the rest of this passage, including the bamboo-skewer argument at the end.

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
One may not prop up the pot with a log,
and similarly the door,
phrases.notes: This matches the corrected reading from step 4.

phrases.english: because wood was not given
except for burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין סוֹמְכִין אֶת הַקְּדֵרָה בַּבְּקַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that states the reason for the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Firewood is designated only for burning, so using it as a prop is forbidden as מוקצה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits propping with wood
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and allows using the log as a prop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא records a dissent. רבי שמעון allows propping a pot or door with a log.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון generally does not accept the rabbinic ban of מוקצה in cases like this. So for him, wood may be used for things other than burning.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who generally does not hold of מוקצה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the תנא קמא in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, a log may be used as a prop because he does not accept מוקצה here.

steps.title: Leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב. But רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new case: driving an animal along with a stick. The first opinion forbids it and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance this looks like the same מוקצה debate, since a stick is a piece of wood. That impression sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון

phrases.english: And one may not lead the animal
with a stick on a Festival,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַנְהִיגִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בַּמַּקֵּל בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a related case about using a stick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: Does the son simply follow his father on מוקצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits because, like his father רבי שמעון, he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like his father, who does not accept מוקצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation for the son's lenient view. This is set up to be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is about מוקצה, then the son is simply following his father's known position. The word 'לימא' signals that this suggestion will likely be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (offers a suggestion that is often rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon
holds like his father,
who does not hold of muktzeh?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן כַּאֲבוּהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what lies behind the dispute in step 7 by linking it to step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute over leading an animal with a stick really a dispute about מוקצה?

steps.title: No: even רבי שמעון forbids this, because it looks like a weekday trip to market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. Here even רבי שמעון agrees the act is forbidden, because it looks like heading to market as on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. In this case even רבי שמעון agrees [that it is forbidden], because it looks like someone going to the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion from step 8. The ban on leading with a stick has nothing to do with מוקצה, so the father-son link does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Driving an animal with a stick looks like taking it to market on a regular weekday, which does not fit the spirit of יום טוב. Since the reason is how it looks and not מוקצה, even רבי שמעון forbids it. So רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's lenient view must be his own, not just his father's view on מוקצה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the stick case is about מוקצה just because a stick is wood. The גמרא says the reason is how the act looks, a weekday-like activity, and that is a separate concern.

phrases.english: No,
in this even Rabbi Shimon agrees,
because it looks
like one who is going to the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying the stick dispute to the מוקצה dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban is about looking like a weekday trip to market, not about מוקצה, so even רבי שמעון agrees with it.

steps.title: A bamboo branch as a skewer: רב נחמן forbids, רב ששת permits
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree about using a bamboo branch (חזרא) as a roasting skewer on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bamboo branch: רב נחמן forbids it, and רב ששת permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute among אמוראים. The question is whether a bamboo branch may be used as a skewer for roasting meat on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The branch was never made into a utensil before יום טוב. So the question is whether using it as a skewer is a forbidden use of wood that is meant only for burning.

keyTerms.meaning: A bamboo or reed-like branch (here, used as a skewer)

phrases.english: A bamboo branch: Rav Nachman forbids,
and Rav Sheshet permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְרָא, רַב נַחְמָן אָסַר, וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new dispute that again involves the rule that wood is only for burning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן forbids using a bamboo branch as a skewer, and רב ששת permits it.

steps.title: Defining the dispute: wet is forbidden by all, dry is debated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the argument. Everyone forbids a wet branch, and the dispute is only about a dry one.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a wet one, everyone agrees it is forbidden. Where they argue is about a dry one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies exactly where the two אמוראים disagree. It rules out the wet branch, which both forbid, and leaves only the dry branch in dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wet branch cannot even be burned, so it has no permitted use at all on יום טוב and is fully מוקצה. A dry branch is usable as fuel, so the question becomes whether that allows it to be used as a skewer too.

phrases.english: With a wet one —
everyone agrees that it is forbidden.
When they argue — it is about a dry one.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרַטִּיבָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute stated in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wet branch is forbidden according to everyone, and the dispute applies only to a dry branch.

steps.title: רב נחמן's reason: wood is only for burning
steps.stepSummary: The one who forbids, רב נחמן, relies on the ברייתא's rule that wood is designated only for burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids would tell you: wood was given only for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב נחמן's view. He applies the same rule used for propping a pot with a log.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, using the branch as a skewer is a use other than burning. So it falls under the same ban as propping a pot with a log in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Would say to you (gives his reasoning)

phrases.english: The one who forbids would say to you:
Wood was given only for burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the stricter side of the dispute narrowed in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dry branch is forbidden as a skewer because wood is designated only for burning.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason: roasting with it is like roasting over its coals
steps.stepSummary: The one who permits, רב ששת, argues that roasting with the branch is no different from burning it and roasting over its coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who permits would tell you: What difference is it to me whether I roast with it, or roast with its coals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב ששת's lenient view in this first version of the dispute. He sees using the branch as a skewer as just another kind of roasting. The next step gives a second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood is meant for cooking, and burning it to roast food is clearly allowed. רב ששת argues that sticking it into meat to roast is the same goal, cooking food, so it is not a forbidden 'other use.' רב נחמן reads 'burning' narrowly as fuel only, while רב ששת reads it broadly as any use for roasting.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is it to me (the two cases are the same)

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, both sides accept that wood is 'only for burning,' and they argue about what that means. רב נחמן says it means fuel only. רב ששת says any roasting use counts, so for him a dry bamboo skewer is allowed. A second version and the final ruling follow in steps 14–16.

phrases.english: And the one who permits would say to you:
What difference is it to me to roast with it,
or to roast with its coals?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּשָׁרֵי, אָמַר לָךְ: מָה לִי לִצְלוֹת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning to step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dry branch may be used as a skewer, because roasting with it is the same as roasting over its coals.

steps.title: A second version: the argument is only about a wet branch
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the רב נחמן and רב ששת dispute says everyone permits a dry branch, and they argue only about a wet one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: with a dry branch, everyone agrees it is permitted. Where they argue is about a wet branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different report (איכא דאמרי) of where exactly רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree. It flips the picture from Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 11), everyone forbade a wet branch and the fight was about a dry one. In this version, everyone permits a dry branch and the fight is about a wet one. So the area of disagreement has moved to the harder case.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions together. Version 1: everyone forbids wet, and they argue about dry. Version 2: everyone permits dry, and they argue about wet. They are opposite maps of the same dispute.

phrases.english: Some say:
phrases.notes: Signals an alternate version of the dispute

phrases.aramaic: בְּיַבִּשְׁתָּא — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: With a dry one, everyone agrees that it is permitted.
Where they argue is about a wet one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing version of the scope of the dispute defined in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Second version: a dry branch is permitted by all, and the dispute concerns only a wet branch.

steps.title: The reasons for each side in the second version
steps.stepSummary: The one who forbids says a wet branch is not fit for burning. The one who permits says it can still burn in a big fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids does so because a wet branch is not fit for kindling. The one who permits would tell you: but it is fit for a big fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side in this second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidding side says that wood counts as usable on יום טוב only because it is fuel, and a wet branch is not good fuel, so it is מוקצה. The permitting side answers that in a large fire even wet wood dries out and burns, so it still counts as fuel and may be handled.

phrases.english: The one who forbids: because it is not fit for kindling.
And the one who permits would say to you:
But it is fit for a large fire!
phrases.notes: A big fire will dry and burn even a wet branch

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reasoning behind both sides of the dispute as framed in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidding view: a wet branch is not fuel. Permitting view: it is fuel for a large fire.

steps.title: Final ruling: dry is permitted, wet is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that a dry branch may be used and a wet one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: a dry one is permitted, a wet one is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole bamboo-branch discussion with a practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling matches the point that both versions share. Dry is permitted, as in version 2 and as רב ששת held in version 1. Wet is forbidden, as in version 1 and as the forbidding side held in version 2. The deciding test is whether the branch is fit to be burned as fuel.
steps.whatToRemember: Bamboo branch as a skewer on יום טוב: dry is permitted, because it is fit for burning. Wet is forbidden, because it is not ready fuel and so is מוקצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the skewer case. A branch may be used for roasting on יום טוב only if it truly counts as fuel. This does not permit other uses of firewood, such as propping a pot or door, which the ברייתא forbids.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: a dry one is permitted,
a wet one is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute presented in both versions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A dry bamboo branch may be used as a skewer on יום טוב. A wet one may not.

steps.title: רבא's two rules about a fire-poker
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a woman may not take a stick from the woodshed to use as a poker, and that a poker that broke on יום טוב may not be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: a woman may not go into the woodshed to take a stick to use as a poker. And a poker that broke may not be burned on יום טוב, because we may burn vessels but we may not burn broken pieces of vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching with two rules about a poker (אוד), the stick used to stir a fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: wood in the woodshed is set aside only for burning, so using it as a tool is not allowed. This matches the idea from Step 12. Rule 2: a poker is a vessel, so it may be burned. Once it breaks, though, the broken pieces are a new thing that came into being on יום טוב, so they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A firebrand or poker used to stir a fire

steps.confusionAlert: The second rule is not saying that burning wood is the problem. A whole poker may be burned, because it is a vessel. Only the broken pieces are forbidden, because they are newly made on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rava taught:
A woman may not enter the woodshed
to take from them a poker.
phrases.notes: Wood there is designated only for burning, not for use as a tool

phrases.aramaic: וְאוּד שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר — אָסוּר לְהַסִּיקוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And a poker that broke may not be burned on יום טוב,
because one may burn vessels,
but one may not burn broken pieces of vessels.
phrases.notes: The shards are a new thing (נולד) that came into existence on יום טוב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related teaching about using wood for something other than burning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood stored for burning may not be taken for use as a poker. A poker that broke on יום טוב may not be burned, because broken pieces of vessels may not be used for fuel.

steps.title: Does רבא hold of מוקצה? He fed goose innards to a cat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבא's rules sound like רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה, yet רבא had goose innards thrown to the cat on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבא agrees with רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה? But רבא told his attendant: roast me a goose, and throw its innards to the cat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between רבא's teaching here and how רבא himself acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rules only make sense if he holds of מוקצה, like רבי יהודה. But according to רבי יהודה, innards that become separated on יום טוב were not prepared for the cat from before, so they should be forbidden to give to it. Yet רבא told his attendant to throw them to the cat.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces an inference to check)
Something set aside and not prepared for use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרָבָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rava holds like רבי יהודה,
who holds of מוקצה?
But Rava said to his attendant:
Roast a goose for me,
and throw its innards to the cat!
phrases.notes: According to רבי יהודה, this should be forbidden as מוקצה

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרָבָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 17 by showing that its assumption seems to contradict רבא's own behavior.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבא holds of מוקצה like רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's rules assume מוקצה, but his practice of giving innards to the cat assumes that there is no מוקצה.

steps.title: Innards spoil, so he had them in mind from the day before
steps.stepSummary: The innards are different. Since they spoil quickly, רבא already planned on the day before to give them to the cat.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, since the innards go bad, from yesterday his mind was already on them for the cat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the goose case is different, so רבא can still hold of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוקצה is about things a person did not have in mind before יום טוב. Everyone knows innards spoil if left, so before יום טוב a person already expects to give them to his animals. That means they are prepared, and they are not מוקצה even according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind was on it (he had it in mind)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא does hold of מוקצה like רבי יהודה. The goose innards are not מוקצה, because they spoil and so were already intended for the animals from before יום טוב.

phrases.english: There, since they spoil,
from yesterday his mind was on them.
phrases.notes: So they were prepared before יום טוב and are not מוקצה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 18 by distinguishing the goose case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (התם שאני: the innards were intended from before יום טוב)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving the innards to the cat shows that רבא does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Innards spoil, so they were expected for the animals before יום טוב and were never מוקצה. רבא can still hold like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי אליעזר permits a toothpick splinter and gathering from the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that a person may take a splinter from what is in front of him to clean his teeth, and may gather kindling from the courtyard, because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: a person may take a splinter from what is in front of him to clean his teeth. And he may gather from the courtyard and light a fire, because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי אליעזר gives two lenient rules about using small pieces of wood on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: a splinter taken from what lies in front of him (such as a pile of straw) may be used as a toothpick. Rule 2: kindling scattered around the courtyard may be gathered and burned. His reason is that anything in the courtyard is considered ready to use.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)
A splinter or chip of wood
To pick or clean (between the teeth)
Prepared, ready for use (the opposite of מוקצה)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: רבי אליעזר says:
A person may take a splinter from what is in front of him,
to clean his teeth with it.
And he may gather from the courtyard and light a fire,
because everything in the courtyard counts as prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה on a related theme: using wood and kindling on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: one may take a splinter for a toothpick and gather kindling from the courtyard, because everything in the courtyard is מוכן.

steps.title: חכמים: gather only from what is in front of you
steps.stepSummary: חכמים are stricter. One may gather and kindle only from what is right in front of him, not from the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: he may gather from what is in front of him and light a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their opinion, which limits רבי אליעזר's ruling about gathering from the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the things in the courtyard do not count as prepared, because a person did not plan before יום טוב to collect scattered pieces from there. Only what is right in front of him in the house is ready for use. The גמרא will go on to clarify how they treat the toothpick case.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: the whole courtyard counts as prepared, so one may gather from there. חכמים: one may gather only from what is right in front of him.

phrases.english: And the חכמים say:
He may gather from what is in front of him and light a fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אליעזר and narrows where one may gather kindling from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: one may gather and kindle only from what is right in front of him. The courtyard is not considered prepared.

steps.title: No producing a new fire on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not produce fire from wood, stones, dirt, tiles, or water.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not produce fire on יום טוב. Not from wood, not from stones, not from dirt, not from tiles, and not from water.
steps.whatsHappening: The same משנה continues with a different rule. It forbids making a brand-new fire on יום טוב and lists five materials that cannot be used to start one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may cook with a fire that is already burning, and you may pass that existing flame along. This משנה forbids creating a new fire from nothing. Examples are rubbing pieces of wood together, striking stones or tiles against each other, or focusing sunlight through a glass vessel of water.

keyTerms.meaning: Producing or bringing out fire, meaning creating a new flame
Pieces of wood, rubbed together to make sparks
Stones, knocked together to make sparks
Water. Here it means water in a round glass vessel that focuses sunlight

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean fire is forbidden on יום טוב. Using a fire that already exists is permitted. Only making a brand-new fire is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known הלכה that on יום טוב you may light a flame from an existing fire, but you may not strike a new one.

phrases.english: One may not produce fire
neither from wood,
phrases.notes: By rubbing one piece against another

phrases.english: nor from stones,
nor from dirt
nor from tiles,
nor from water.
phrases.notes: In a round glass vessel that focuses the sun's rays

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same משנה moves to a new topic. Steps 20–21 discussed gathering kindling for an existing fire. This step forbids creating a new fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not create a new fire by any method: wood, stones, dirt, tiles, or water.

steps.title: No heating tiles white-hot to roast on
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that one may not heat tiles until they turn white in order to roast food on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not heat tiles until they turn white in order to roast food on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second rule. You may not heat tiles until they are white-hot so that you can later roast food on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds like normal cooking preparation, which is usually allowed on יום טוב. Even so, the משנה forbids it. The גמרא will soon explain what is wrong with heating the tiles this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Whitening, meaning heating something until it glows white-hot

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two rules. You may not create a new fire on יום טוב. You may not heat tiles white-hot in order to roast on them.

phrases.english: And one may not whiten tiles
phrases.notes: By heating them until they glow white-hot

phrases.english: to roast upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְלַבְּנִין אֶת הָרְעָפִים לִצְלוֹת בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step adds a second ruling to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not heat tiles white-hot on יום טוב in order to roast food on them.

steps.title: The גמרא opens with רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by quoting רב יהודה. His actual statement comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its first move on this משנה. It introduces a statement by רב יהודה, and his actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only tells us who is speaking. This passage ends before we hear the content. Expect רב יהודה to explain or clarify one of the rulings in the משנה we just read.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא. It marks where the discussion of the משנה begins
A leading Babylonian אמורא, a student of רב and שמואל

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step moves from the text of the משנה to the start of the גמרא's discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the attribution appears here. רב יהודה's actual teaching continues on the next amud.
